title: What Is a Content Pillar and How Do You Build One? (August 2026)
summary: Learn what a content pillar is, see real examples, and follow a step-by-step guide to building one for your strategy in July 2026.
body_text: Most content strategies have the ingredients. They don't have the structure. You've got posts on related topics, a few solid long-form guides, maybe even some decent keyword research, but none of those pages are intentionally linked together around a central pillar. You're leaving ranking power sitting on the table. Here's what that structure actually looks like, and how to build it. TLDR: A content pillar is a single long-form page targeting a broad keyword; a topic cluster is the group of supporting pages around it. Internal linking between pillar and cluster pages is what signals topical authority to Google, not the content alone. Build pillar topics specific enough to rank but broad enough to support 10 or more cluster posts. Content updated within the past 3 months averages 6 AI citations vs. 3.6 for outdated content, so freshness is a ranking signal now. Maintouch identifies subtopic gaps, generates cluster content, and wires internal linking so pillar structures compound instead of decay. What Is a Content Pillar? Definition and Core Concepts "Content pillar" is one of those terms that means two different things depending on who's using it. Neither camp seems to realize the other exists. In SEO, a content pillar is a long-form page that covers a broad topic thoroughly and links out to narrower cluster posts underneath it. The pillar page owns the big keyword; the cluster pages target more specific queries and link back to the pillar. In brand and social media contexts, a content pillar is a recurring theme or category that shapes what you publish. A B2B company might have pillars like "product education," "customer stories," and "industry trends" (a core part of any B2B SEO marketing strategy ). These aren't pages. They're editorial guardrails that keep your feed from feeling random. Both definitions are valid. The SEO version is structural, built to help search engines understand your site's topical depth. The brand version is editorial, built to keep messaging consistent across channels. I'll focus mostly on the SEO side, but I'll cover social media pillars too. Content Pillars vs. Topic Clusters People use these terms interchangeably, but they describe different parts of the same structure. A content pillar is a single page. A topic cluster is the group of pages that surrounds it. Think of it as hub and spokes. The pillar page covers a broad subject (like "content marketing"), deep enough to be useful on its own and wide enough to branch into subtopics. Each cluster page takes one of those subtopics ("how to write a content brief," "content marketing metrics") and goes narrow and specific. Every cluster page links back to the pillar. The pillar links out to each cluster page. The internal linking pattern is what gives the whole thing its SEO value. Search engines crawl those links and read them as a signal that your site has real depth on the subject, the same signal an SEO AI agent is built to strengthen. Without the linking structure, you've got a collection of loosely related posts. With it, you've got a topical authority play. Why Content Pillars Matter for SEO Content pillars give search engines a clear map of your site's expertise. Organize related pages around a single authoritative pillar, and you're telling Google exactly what you know and how deeply you know it. The SEO payoff comes from three things: Topical authority signals compound as you publish cluster content that links back to the pillar, reinforcing the main page's relevance for competitive head terms. Internal link equity flows deliberately from cluster pages to the pillar, concentrating ranking power where it matters most. Search intent coverage expands because each cluster post targets a specific long-tail query, pulling in traffic the pillar page alone would miss. Sites that build this structure rank for more keywords per topic than sites publishing disconnected posts with no linking logic between them. The gap compounds over time. Types of Content Pillars SEO pillars and brand pillars each come in a few distinct formats. Pick the wrong one and you're burning effort on structure that won't hold. Type Format Best For In-depth guide (10x page) Single long-form page covering a topic end to end Ranking for high-volume head terms like "email marketing" Resource hub page Curated page linking out to the best content on a subject Sites with an existing library of posts that need a central index Pillar with linked subtopics Broad overview page connected to dedicated cluster posts Building topical authority over time as you publish new cluster content On the brand and social side, the categories are thematic, not structural: Educational pillars teach your audience something (tutorials, how-tos, industry breakdowns). Promotional pillars showcase your product or offer. Community pillars build connection through shared values, behind-the-scenes content, or culture. User-generated pillars amplify what your customers create. Most B2B companies running an SEO program will land on the pillar-with-linked-subtopics model because it scales naturally, especially when combined with programmatic SEO tools . You don't need a 5,000-word guide on day one. Publish the pillar, add cluster posts over time, and the structure compounds. Content Pillar Examples A few real examples worth studying: Mailchimp built an "email marketing" pillar page that links out to dozens of cluster posts covering deliverability, segmentation, A/B testing, and list hygiene. The pillar owns the head term; the clusters pull in long-tail traffic and feed authority back up. HubSpot runs separate pillar hubs for "marketing," "sales," and "service," each with its own cluster map. Their site architecture is practically a textbook for this model. Salesforce treats "CRM," "digital transformation," and "customer success" as both SEO pillars on their blog and thematic brand pillars across LinkedIn and their resource library. The pattern is the same regardless of industry: one broad page, many supporting pages, deliberate links tying it together. Social Media Content Pillars A lot of the search volume around "content pillars" comes from social media marketers, not SEO folks. On Instagram, LinkedIn, and TikTok, pillars aren't pages. They're the three to five recurring themes you commit to so your feed has a recognizable rhythm. A B2B service company on LinkedIn might rotate between thought leadership, client results, and team culture. An ecommerce brand on Instagram might cycle through product education, behind-the-scenes, and user-generated content. The number matters less than the consistency: pick too many and your feed feels scattered, pick too few and it gets monotonous fast. How to Build a Content Pillar Strategy: Step by Step Start with who you're writing for. Pull questions from sales calls, support tickets, and Search Console queries longer than ten words. Those tell you what your audience actually wants answered. The best keyword research tools fill in the gaps your own data misses. Then audit what you've already published. Look for posts that overlap in topic or compete for the same keywords and group them. If a natural hub takes shape, that's your pillar candidate. Pick pillar topics broad enough to support ten or more cluster pieces but specific enough to be winnable. "Marketing" is too wide. "Content marketing for B2B SaaS" is ownable. Map each cluster post to a single subtopic under the pillar, then build the links: every cluster page points back to the pillar, every pillar page links out to each cluster. That's the whole architecture. How to Create a Pillar Page Cover each subtopic with enough depth to be useful on its own. Don't go so deep that you cannibalize your cluster posts, and watch for AI slop when drafting at scale. If a subtopic needs more than a few paragraphs to do it justice, it deserves its own page. Add a clickable table of contents at the top so readers (and crawlers) can jump to specific sections. Keep the page ungated. Search engines can't index what sits behind a form, and Portent's 2024 data showed a 207% increase in organic sessions for content hubs built this way. Target your broadest keyword on the pillar. Let each cluster page own one long-tail variation. Keeping Content Pillars Fresh and Performing A pillar page that sits untouched for a year loses ground fast. Content decay is real: pages updated within the past three months receive an Datadab's AI citation data , and roughly half of all AI-cited content is less than 13 weeks old. That's not a minor edge. It's a structural advantage you're either building or ceding. A practical refresh means swapping stale statistics, adding links to new cluster posts, tightening internal links so nothing's orphaned, and updating metadata to reflect the current date. AI-powered content creation speeds up each of those tasks considerably. Freshness is a ranking and citation signal. Treat it that way. How Maintouch Builds and Maintains Content Pillars Automatically Most teams treat content pillars as a one-time project. Build the page, publish the clusters, move on. I've watched good pillar structures decay because nobody owned the ongoing work: new cluster posts never got linked in, the pillar itself went stale, and eventually the whole thing lost ground to a competitor who just kept publishing. I built Maintouch to handle that ongoing work. The content agent identifies subtopic gaps around your core pillars, generates cluster content to fill them, and wires the internal linking together so every new page feeds authority back up. When search behavior changes or new long-tail queries surface, the Content Updates System picks those up and fills them in. No editorial calendar required. If you want to see how it works on your site, shoot me a message at [email protected] . Final Thoughts on What Content Pillars Are and How to Use Them The structure is simple: broad page on top, cluster posts underneath, internal links tying it together. What makes it work long-term isn't the build. It's the maintenance. Keep the pillar fresh, keep publishing cluster content, and the ranking power compounds. Let it sit, and a competitor who kept publishing will eventually take what you built. FAQ What's the difference between a content pillar and a topic cluster? A content pillar is a single page. A topic cluster is the full group of pages surrounding it, including the pillar and all its connected cluster posts. The pillar covers a broad subject; each cluster post targets one specific subtopic and links back to the pillar. Without that internal linking structure, you have loosely related posts. With it, you have a topical authority play that search engines read as genuine depth. How do I choose the right pillar topics for my site? Pick topics broad enough to support ten or more cluster pieces but specific enough to be winnable. "Marketing" is too wide. "Content marketing for B2B SaaS" is ownable. Pull candidate topics from sales call transcripts, support tickets, and Search Console queries longer than ten words. Those sources tell you what your audience actually wants answered, which is a far better signal than keyword volume alone. What should a pillar page actually include to rank and get cited? A strong pillar page runs 3,000 to 5,000 words, covers each subtopic with enough depth to be useful on its own, and includes a clickable table of contents at the top. Keep it ungated so search engines can index it. Target your broadest keyword on the pillar itself and let each cluster page own one long-tail variation. Content updated within the past 90 days gets cited by AI engines at roughly twice the rate of stale pages, so freshness isn't optional. Pillar and cluster content strategy vs. just publishing standalone posts? The pillar-and-cluster model wins on topical authority because the internal linking pattern concentrates ranking power on your most competitive head terms while cluster posts pull in long-tail traffic the pillar alone would miss. Standalone posts with no linking logic between them give search engines no signal about your site's depth on a subject. The structural difference compounds over time: every new cluster post you add feeds authority back to the pillar, so the longer you build the system, the harder it is for competitors to displace you. How does Maintouch handle content pillar maintenance compared to doing it manually? Manual pillar maintenance breaks down because most teams treat the initial build as a one-time project and let the structure decay. Maintouch identifies subtopic gaps around your core SEO pillars, generates cluster content to fill them, and wires internal linking together automatically so every new page feeds authority back to the pillar. When search behavior changes or new long-tail queries surface, the system picks those up without you managing an editorial calendar. The content update queue also flags pillar pages with declining impressions after 90 days and refreshes copy, metadata, and internal links automatically.

title: Payroll Solutions for Nigerian Businesses: How to Choose the Right Platform
summary: Product Payroll Solutions for Nigerian Businesses: How to Choose the Right Platform Oluwakemi Adesina July 13, 2026 Payroll solutions for Nigerian businesses aren’t a nice-to-have anymore. They separate a finance team that sleeps well on salary day from one that doesn’t. If you’ve ever seen a spreadsheet formula break an hour before payday, you know why this matters. Every growing business hits the same wall eventually. The headcount that fits on one screen now needs three tabs. The pension remittance that took ten minutes now takes all afternoon. The HR manager who once knew everyone’s salary from memory now double-checks numbers at 11pm, hoping nobody notices the delay. This is when a business quietly outgrows manual payroll, and it usually happens faster than expected. Manual payroll works for businesses with five people and probably a spreadsheet or just bank transfers. It stops working once operations get more complicated: new hires, exits, loan deductions, pension contributions, tax changes, multiple bank accounts, and the founder asking for a report by Friday. This is where automation proves its value; it handles payroll tasks that do not need constant human attention. What Do Payroll Solutions for Nigerian Businesses Actually Include? A payroll solution is software that calculates what employees are owed, deducts what the law requires, pays everyone correctly, and keeps a clean record of everything. That sounds simple until you run payroll for a 40-person team with different salary structures, join dates, and statutory obligations. A proper payroll management system typically handles four things: salary computation, statutory deductions (tax, pension, NHF), payment disbursement, and reporting. Most payroll software used by Nigerian businesses follows a similar rhythm regardless of provider. HR confirms headcount and changes for the month. The system calculates gross-to-net pay automatically. Deductions are applied per employee. Salaries go out in one batch instead of one bank transfer at a time. For a business owner, that means spending twenty minutes on payroll instead of a full day. Signs Your Business Has Outgrown Manual Payroll One of the major signs is that salaries start going out a day or two late. Someone finds a pension remittance miscalculated three months earlier. A new employee’s first salary is wrong because a formula didn’t update. Reporting for the board or an auditor takes a week instead of an afternoon. None of these are one-off mistakes; they’re symptoms. Businesses growing past 15–20 employees almost always hit this wall because manual processes don’t scale with headcount; they get slower and riskier. A retail chain expanding from two branches in Lagos to eight across the country will feel this almost overnight: more staff, locations, bank accounts, and a payroll spreadsheet never built to handle any of it. This is the clearest signal it’s time to switch to proper business payroll software, long before a growing team scrambles for a payroll platform in which Nigerian businesses can trust under pressure. Key Features Every Payroll Solution Should Have Payroll automation that calculates gross-to-net pay without manual formulas Automatic statutory deductions for tax, pension, and NHF, updated when regulations change Bulk salary payments that disburse to every employee’s bank account in one transaction Employee self-service for payslips, leave, and personal records Reporting dashboards that generate compliance and finance reports on demand Common Mistakes Businesses Make When Choosing Payroll Software Choosing Based on Pricing: The most common mistake is choosing based on price alone. The cheapest payroll software might skip statutory updates, leaving the business responsible for catching compliance errors manually. This defeats the purpose of automation. Businesses comparing quotes on price alone usually discover this gap only when the first compliance query arrives from a regulator. By then, switching payroll software midyear is far more disruptive than choosing carefully the first time. Ignoring scalability: A payroll management system that works for 10 employees might buckle at 100, especially if it wasn’t built for Nigerian payroll structures from day one. Choosing a system with no integrations: This forces HR to manually transfer data between HR, finance, and payroll tools. Weak compliance support: This leaves a business exposed when tax regulations change. At some point, the cost of not having proper business payroll software outweighs the monthly subscription cost. How the Right Payroll Solutions for Nigerian Businesses Improve Operations When payroll works as it should, the effect shows up everywhere in the business. Finance teams stop reconciling numbers manually. HR stops fielding “where’s my salary” messages. Employees get paid correctly and on time, which builds trust in an employer more than any perk. Compliance stops being a monthly fire drill when statutory deductions are calculated the first time correctly. This is what good payroll automation software should do: work in the background. An HR payroll solution that automates all this doesn’t just save hours. It removes an entire category of risk from the business. Why Businesses Choose Eazipay Eazipay is a digital payroll solution built specifically for Nigerian payroll. It automates salary calculations, statutory deductions, and bulk salary payments in one platform, so businesses aren’t stitching together three separate tools to get one job done. Eazipay handles payroll, compliance, and employee management so you don’t have to. We end the stress of payday and protect your business from penalties. Along with an HR payroll solution that keeps employee records up to date and provides payroll reports whenever finance needs them, Eazipay offers your growing business a payroll platform you can rely on as you expand. title: Roblox 的「家庭專區」協助親子共同探索
summary: Family Zone, a game built by Roblox and developer MindTrust, fosters co-play between children and their parents and facilitates conversations about digital safety in an entertaining way.
body_text: 分享 新聞 安全與文明 Roblox 的「家庭專區」協助親子共同探索 讓家長以有趣且互動的方式，與孩子的網路世界建立連結 發佈者 塔米・巴烏米克（Tami Bhaumik），禮儀與合作關係副總裁 發佈日期 2026年7月14日 今天我們推出「Family Zone」，這是一款由 Roblox 與開發商 MindTrust 共同打造的遊戲，旨在讓家長和照顧者更了解該平台。「Family Zone」促進親子共同遊玩，並以寓教於樂的方式引導關於數位安全的對話。 這款遊戲旨在彌合代溝，讓家長能透過有趣、安全且積極的方式，在數位世界中與孩子共同遊玩並增進親子情感 。 在遊戲中，家長與孩子將一同學習平台基礎知識，例如如何在 3D 空間中操控虛擬角色，以及如何設定和調整家長控制功能。他們還能了解更廣泛的網路安全主題，這些內容旨在提升玩家在 Roblox 以外網站的數位素養。 我們開發「Family Zone」，是因為了解 Roblox 的最佳方式就是親自遊玩。雖然多數家長都有玩線上遊戲的經驗，但許多人對 Roblox 的遊戲內容與設定仍不熟悉，這可能限制他們能否在充分了解的情況下有效運用家長控制功能。「Family Zone」旨在透過親身體驗所獲得的理解，協助促進家長與孩子之間的持續對話 Family Zone 顛覆了傳統的學習模式。孩子會引導父母在平台上邁出第一步，示範如何在數位空間中移動與探索。當父母跟著孩子的引導操作時，便能完全掌控虛擬角色的動作與導航。 「家庭專區」透過互動式課程，讓家長深入了解安全知識，並認識 Roblox 業界領先的安全防護機制與功能。我們引導家長使用強大的家長控制功能，讓已綁定帳戶的家長能設定螢幕使用時間限制、管理消費、選擇孩子可聯繫的對象，以及管理孩子可遊玩的游戏。我們為完成遊戲內教學的玩家提供獎勵（例如獨家虛擬角色道具），並為家庭提供多種適合各年齡層的體驗。 我們正與全球安全專家及頂尖組織合作，設計可透過「家庭專區」存取的額外模組，涵蓋防範詐騙、網路霸凌，以及識別與避免掠食性行為等關鍵議題。例如，我們正與領先的心理健康非營利組織 Koko 、 Playerthree ，以及西北大學「 可擴展心理健康實驗室 」的頂尖研究人員合作，設計一款遊戲，協助兒童和青少年在面對霸凌時培養韌性。 「Family Zone」將持續新增教育內容及共同遊玩機會，讓家庭能一起在 Roblox 上享受嶄新的體驗。

title: Astec Ambition Shines Bright in the Hillhead 2026 Sunshine
summary: With eight new products and patented technology across two large stands and in the Demo Area, Astec made a big statement at Hillhead 2026.
body_text: Home Resources News Press Releases Astec Ambition Shines Bright in the Hillhead 2026 Sunshine Press Releases Astec Ambition Shines Bright in the Hillhead 2026 Sunshine With eight new products and patented technology innovations spread across two large stands… July 10, 2026 Share: With eight new products and patented technology innovations spread across two large stands and in the ‘Crusher Alley’ Rock Processing Demo Area, Astec made a big statement at Hillhead 2026 with its ambitious growth plans in Europe and the rest of the world, built on its rich 150-year engineering history. At Astec’s Day 1 exhibition press conference, attendees heard that the company’s new product line is focused on innovation and application. This includes new washing plants, material handling equipment, screening technology, and mobile crushing and screening units. The eight products on show at Hillhead 2026 (23-25 June) are among more than 20 that will enter the quarrying, roadbuilding, construction, and recycling markets over the next two years. The Astec senior management team panel of Jaco Van Der Merwe, CEO; Michael Norris, Group President Materials Solutions; Damian Power, Managing Director, Astec Europe; Stephen Whyte, Vice President, Product Management; and Malachy Gribben, Vice President, Channel Management stressed how the company’s investment in its Omagh, County Tyrone, Northern Ireland, facility has established a strong European footprint, enabling local manufacturing of the new Frontier range of tracked crushing and screening units unveiled at Hillhead 2026. “We are global but local in Europe,” said Damian Power. “We have 230 people in our Omagh facility, across manufacturing, engineering and product support. We now have a critical mass for product support and parts and service in the European region. This facility was built with expansion in mind, offering a runway for growth over the next five years.” Astec differentiates itself through unique product features, including its patented Multi-Frequency Screen, which addresses blinding issues, and its new patented Vari LPV screen, which represents next-generation technology. Stephen Whyte said, “If you look around some of the products here, there are not many companies in our industry that have the level of NPD [New Product Development], either completed in recent years or ongoing, that we do.” Further emphasising how Astec stands out in a highly competitive crushing and screening solution marketplace, Jaco Van Der Merwe said, “Customers buy the whole team, not just the equipment. That includes the dealer network, some of whom we have here, who are among the best people in the industry. We are a parts and service business that sells equipment, and if we provide that to our customers, the features and benefits you see on every other machine [at Hillhead 2026] become a whole lot less important.” The European quarrying sector has faced challenges in recent years, but Malachy Gribben said Astec sees significant growth opportunities and projects an upward trend in aggregate production over the next three to five years. The company aims to increase its market share in Europe, even in a soft market. “We see the bright lights of opportunity,” stressed Gribben. “There are some big markets in Europe, such as Germany, but establishing a strong base here in the UK will be a firm start for us,” said Van Der Merwe, who, when asked a question on whether Astec’s engineering heritage, dating back to 1876, will be a notable benefit in executing its European growth strategy, responded, “We have done this for a while. We are definitely not a new player in the market. Our legacy was built on innovation and customer service, and that is what we bring to Europe, and it is an offer that will work anywhere in the world.” During the press conference, attendees heard Jaco Van Der Merwe highlight that Astec, a major U.S.-headquartered off-highway equipment manufacturer with a 4,500-strong global workforce, is actively pursuing growth in Europe through organic development and strategic acquisitions, leveraging a strong balance sheet. Astec’s CEO said the company’s acquisitions will focus on areas within its core business, such as crushing, asphalt, and concrete equipment, to bolster its European platform. Jaco Van Der Merwe and Stephen White explained how customer needs are evolving towards lower cost per tonne, driven by challenges such as labour shortages and rising fuel and energy costs. Astec is responding with more efficient equipment, digital telematics-based platforms for remote monitoring and predictive maintenance, and a focus on energy efficiency. The Signal connectivity suite from Astec Digital delivers seamless communication and monitoring across all customer plant and mobile assets, generating actionable insights to boost efficiency, productivity and profitability. “If you look at our Signal platform, you can compare it to the Apple environment, with your MacBook, your iPad and your iPhone, which are all working in the same connectivity suite. A lot of our customers work across the aggregates, asphalt, concrete, and paving spaces, and we can provide them with a digital resource to drive their businesses,” explained Michael Norris. At the Hillhead 2026 press conference, attendees heard how Astec is integrating AI and automation across its operations, from product development (predictive maintenance, autonomous breakers) to business processes (energy efficiency calculators, AI-driven vision systems for asphalt plants). Jaco Van Der Merwe highlighted Astec DropZone, an intelligent, AI-powered load-out safety system designed to streamline asphalt delivery and prevent costly misloads. It replaces manual silo loading by utilising computer vision to precisely verify truck positioning beneath the silo, safeguarding both drivers and equipment. The press conference heard how Astec is also investing in training its leadership in AI. As Astec’s senior management team emphasised, the company’s Hillhead 2026 showcase focused on solving real operational challenges by reducing downtime, improving throughput, and lowering cost per tonne. As well as Hillhead 2026, marking the European launch of the new Frontier tracked mobile crushing and screening range, built for flexibility, fast setup, and high-performance production in demanding hard rock environments, Astec staged the global launch of the Kolberg Washing brand and featured the Eco-Scrub modular washing solution, delivering wet processing with a design especially suited for semi-mobile locations. The exhibition launch of Astec’s Modex brand, displaying the patented Vari-Frequency Technology, which minimises binding and maximises output, was showcased on Astec Modex’s Pioneer 6203LPV horizontal screen. Proven for over two decades on tough materials and unveiled in Europe at Hillhead 2026, Astec’s Multi-Frequency Screen is available on tracks, wheels or static, and notably reduces blinding even with sticky materials. In certain applications the product can produce manufactured sand from CRF (Crushed Rock Fines) without washing and turn quarry scalpings into saleable products. It is also well-suited for RAP (Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement), topsoil, compost, and skip waste fines. Celebrating 25 years Astec’s Telestack brand was also well represented at Hillhead 2026, with the worldwide launch of the LF527 low feed hopper, which reduces double handling and ensures smooth, controlled material flow, and the TCL 1031 Zero, a heavy-duty stacker engineered to handle high tonnage reliably and efficiently. Furthermore, ‘Crusher Alley’ attendees watched Astec’s Frontier JA45 Mobile Jaw delivering consistent, high-output crushed aggregate to the Frontier SDF16 Mobile Scalper, resulting in multiple products with peerless flexibility. Astec recently appointed Red Knight 6 (England and Wales) and O’Kane Equipment Solutions (Scotland and Northern England) as its official GB distributors for the new Frontier tracked crushing and screening brand. The press conference heard how both distributors bring deep industry knowledge and strong customer relationships, making them ideal partners for Astec and its globally recognised engineering and UK-manufactured equipment. Commenting on Astec’s approach to growing its European distributor network, Malachy Gribben said, “You walk around this quarry [at Hillhead 2026] and see line after line of crushing and screening plant. We invested a lot of time and effort talking to the European market and industry stakeholders, including end users and potential dealers, and asking, ‘What’s going on in your world and where do you see things going?’ One very consistent message was that those stakeholders were seeing less and less differentiation in the market. Like everything else, when you’re buying a crusher or a car, you want choice. We quickly realised that if we could offer a proven and credible alternative, not just on the product side, but also in parts and service, and a team that truly walks in the shoes of the customer, we would stand out.” Asked about what Red Knight 6 and O’Kane Equipment Solutions will bring to Astec’s offer to UK customers, Gribben responded, “Although the announcement has been made within the last couple of months, we have been working closely together for the last couple of years. Their strong relationships with customers and within the wider industry are clear, and they have a similar outlook to ours.” Stephen Whyte added that, as part of its wider company development programme, Astec works with customer and dealer advocacy groups worldwide to ensure its product and service offerings meet market needs. Speaking from the press conference attendee floor and responding to a question on whether Astec still had gaps in its product and linked technologies range, Paul Donnelly, managing director of Red Knight 6, said, ‘It’s the others [OEMs] that have gaps. Kieran [O’Kane, MD O’Kane Equipment Solutions] and I both have 30 years in the industry and have lived with some many changes and false dawns. With the technologies Astec have, such as the Multi-Frequency Screen, we’ve been testing it here in the UK, and Astec is doing things others can’t. It’s exciting for us as dealers. Equipment costs have risen significantly, customers are not getting much more money for the material they are extracting from the ground, so equipment now has to last five or six years, when before it was financed in a three-year cycle. Quality build and innovation is why Astec is the partner we want to work with.” Share: About Astec Since 1972, Astec Industries, Inc. has been connecting communities by providing innovative rock to road solutions for our customers. United by our purpose – Built to Connect – Astec is a leading global manufacturer of specialized equipment for asphalt road building, aggregate processing and concrete production. Operations are divided into two primary business segments. Infrastructure Solutions includes road building, asphalt and concrete plants, thermal and storage solutions. Materials Solutions includes aggregate and other material processing solutions. For more information, follow us on social media.

title: Why getting your data in order is key to enabling “speed to trusted action” for the energy transition
summary: Utilities are dealing with exponential growth in the volume and complexity of data. At the same time, they are readying for the energy transition by preparing networks to support electrification and increased use of renewable energy resources, like wind, solar and tidal, which are intermittent and less dependable. To be successful, utility leaders need to make the right decisions at the right time. This requires data to be at the heart of the decision-making process. It must be accurate, reliable, complete, relevant and timely to help guide and prioritize decisions.
body_text: Utilities are dealing with exponential growth in the volume and complexity of data. At the same time, they are readying for the energy transition by preparing networks to support electrification and increased use of renewable energy resources, like wind, solar and tidal, which are intermittent and less dependable. To be successful, utility leaders need to make the right decisions at the right time. This requires data to be at the heart of the decision-making process. It must be accurate, reliable, complete, relevant and timely to help guide and prioritize decisions. Effective data governance—which defines how an organization produces and consumes data while being organized to make data-driven decisions—is essential to achieving these requirements. Data governance that enables “speed to trusted action”—not restriction—is the key to success. The energy future depends on data All elements of the energy transition are increasingly dependent on data: Future system-wide access with local flexibility (e.g., distributed resources, smart photovoltaic inverters, battery storage, smart EV charging, and more) requires reliable and real-time data to manage the connected distribution system, avoid congestion on the distribution grids, postpone investment while maximizing the use of distribution assets, and integrate renewable energy sources. Integrated network management solutions , like distributed energy resource management systems (DERMS) and advanced distribution management systems (ADMS), use advanced data analytics to support grid operators and advanced grid planning solutions. This helps distribution system design engineers prioritize grid investments (e.g., prediction tools to improve maintenance predictability of energy assets). Improving the customer experience and engagement , new customer platforms, and innovative approaches to attract and retain customers in DER programs requires actionable data, as does asset maintenance, repairs, upgrade plans, replacements for obsolescence, predictive maintenance and overall asset management. Activating climate pledges calls for building, connecting and tracking sustainability data across the value chain to measure and demonstrate progress, track goals and make informed decisions on how to decarbonize buildings and fleets and embed new ways of working to advance ESG goals. Uncertainty has some utilities performing a balancing act While all of the above is "within reach," there is uncertainty about the nature and pace of these initiatives. For instance, while intermittent generation is increasing steadily, the adoption rate of electrification and distributed generation—which could lead to voltage violation on distribution networks—is unclear. None of these has reached a point yet where they are truly disruptive to the grid. As a result, some utilities are taking a cautious and balanced stance, preparing for the energy transition but remaining agile in their technology investments to develop the data capabilities needed to support transformation. However, utilities executives know that electrification and distributed generation can quickly accelerate and likely will be adopted in clusters across the distribution network, which will compound their impact. Getting your data in order What can you do now to prepare for the upcoming changes? A key first step is to get your data in order. Effective data governance supports business strategy and objectives by determining how data management activities must be operationalized within the organization and across its ecosystem. It provides the management framework that ensures shared responsibility for data-related decisions through a detailed, accurate and integrated view of data. This requires: Envisioning the role of data in adapting business and operating models to meet the challenges of the energy transition Considering the strategic role of data management (this often is overlooked) Making a paradigm shift from highly formatted data to open and shared data, as this may be the preference of future legal and regulatory frameworks Enabling better collaboration, especially across organizational silos and between multiple market actors (e.g., transmission system operators, distribution system operators, generators, end users, aggregators, etc.) Improving agility and resilience in decision-making to embrace changing market trends, i.e., increased “speed to trusted action" Benefits of data governance Data governance is successful when fully integrated with business operations. It provides a holistic view of data-related business and technology activities to support effective decision-making in the face of transformation challenges. Specific benefits include: Decision-maker empowerment – Utilities executives need to make decisions faster and more efficiently by relying on reliable data models (i.e., ensuring integrated and appropriate network modeling) and leveraging data assets (e.g., reduced IT maintenance and increased analytics). Strategic alignment – Data governance can help utilities executives benefit greatly by ensuring data models and associated data assets are aligned with the organization’s needs and vision. It can reduce the cost and time to deploy solutions such as energy efficiency and demand response programs, marketing and customer engagement programs, DERMS and ADMS and improve effectiveness through enhanced operational excellence. Increased collaboration – Integrated and structured data governance across the utility enables better communication and collaboration between traditionally siloed teams and across market stakeholders. It also supports synergies between IT and business to effectively modernize information systems (e.g., data hubs, real-time demand response, etc.) and better control data assets (e.g., data analytics to support CAPEX and OPEX planning). Closer partnerships also improve operational efficiency (e.g., better security network systems and protection, reduced maintenance, etc.) and anticipation of transformation needs (e.g., phasing out security systems exposed to performance, security and legal risks). Continuous business process improvement – Data governance provides the management framework to identify the root causes that can affect operational efficiency and help prioritize decisions. It provides an opportunity to engage diverse teams to understand how data is used and how to use it better to drive change. Using data governance to enable more inclusive and integrated business processes empowers utilities to better identify improvement opportunities. For instance, how to integrate technologies, such as DERMS, with traditional system engineering and planning, or advanced demand forecasting tools to achieve business goals faster, or how to accelerate cloud modernization to unlock the potential of your energy assets. Modern data architecture – A key aspect of effective data governance is a modern data architecture to overcome data silos by providing an integrated view of critical data that resides in multiple systems, including legacy systems. Data governance promotes business-IT collaboration to maximize the value and diversity of data needed to manage networks effectively. For example, using the same dataset to run a predictive model to automate transport and distributed system design engineering, detect assets at risk of network outages, support equipment maintenance and prioritize work. We invite you to listen to the Energy Transition podcast – A perfect storm for data and analytics to be the future of energy and utilities – by our colleagues on data governance and enablement for more perspectives on this topic and to contact us to discuss how we can work together to support your data journey.
